lines.text: In 1975, one guy sold ordinary beach stones as pets â€”
and became a millionaire in six months.
See, copywriter Gary Dahl got tired of friends complaining about walking dogs,
so he joked the perfect pet wouldn't need food, baths, or vet bills.
So he bought plain stones for a penny each,
tucked them onto straw inside tiny cardboard pet carriers,
complete with air holes so they could breathe.
Even better, he wrote a funny thirty-two-page care manual,
explaining how to teach your stone to sit and stay.
Then he slapped a four-dollar price tag on every box.
Shoppers went completely wild before Christmas,
buying one point five million literal rocks.
People laughed at the gimmick all the way to the register,
while Gary Dahl laughed all the way to the bank.
